bounded_question: What does the stats-snapshot insert 0x606ef50 build from a source iterator, how does its caller 0x5d4cc80 create and hand off the snapshot node, and what do the two node types (vtables 0x64d2c28/0x64d2c90) differ in?

arguments: r8: snapshot slot (pointer to node pointer)

wrapper.rule: wrapper(node): rsi = 1 + count_getter(node), rdx = *(node+0x18), tail-jump to insert

layout.+0x08: bound / first-entry sequence: flag-nonzero path zeroes it; flag-0 path leaves the fresh allocation until the locked lookup writes it on success; insert overwrites it with the first parsed key-prefix sequence
layout.+0x20: payload: flag-0 path written by map_copy on lookup success, else fresh-allocation contents; flag-nonzero path unwritten
layout.+0x28: embedded std::map header: color +0x28 (u32 0), parent +0x30, left +0x38, right +0x40, count +0x48
layout.+0x50: u32, zeroed at build; copied into the owner by slot 7
layout.+0x54: u16, zeroed at build; copied into the owner by slot 7
layout.+0x58: char*, zeroed at build; strdup-copied into the owner by slot 7
layout.+0x60: flag byte: 1 while the snapshot is live, 0 on the early exits

slot_meanings.0: destructor: free +0x58 array, then free every map entry (key dispose A 0x606c280 / B 0x606def0)
slot_meanings.1: deleting destructor: slot 0 then operator delete(node, 0x70)
slot_meanings.3: refresh: A calls node_init(node, 1+*(node+0x8), *(node+0x18)); B tail-jumps to insert(node, 1+*(node+0x8), *(node+0x18))
slot_meanings.7: copy header: owner u32@0 = node u32@0x50, owner u16@4 = node u16@0x54, owner ptr@8 = strdup(node ptr@0x58) (old owner ptr freed); returns owner

node.type_select: flag *(source+0x4c9) == 0 selects type A, != 0 selects type B

insert.null_source: node+0x68 == 0: node+0x60 = 0 and return (no map change)
insert.state_init: 0x60b21f0 fills a 0x90-byte struct: all zero except +0x2c = 0x101, +0x78 = -1, +0x84 = 4, +0x88 = 0x100; the second argument is ignored
insert.bound_getter: 0x5d532d0 returns *(source+0xac0), passed as the third argument to the slot-0x198 produce call
insert.seek_value: max(node+0x8, bound) formatted into an 11-byte buffer (10 digits, NUL at +10)
insert.first_entry: parsed once before the loop: node+0x8 = its key-prefix sequence; if node+0x8 < bound the flag is cleared, the iterator released and the routine returns without touching the map
per_entry: parse the current key view with the delimited-key parser 0x606eb60 (bound = insert bound)
move the parsed suffix into the saved-key slot (rsp+0xb8)
skip the entry when the saved key is exactly the 35-byte format-version key (advance via slot 0x38)
read the value view via slot 0x50, copy it into a string with the hex helper flag-0 path, decimal-parse it with 0x61d1540 into the sequence
lower-bound walk + 0x5d6c600: an exact duplicate key is dropped (first occurrence wins); otherwise allocate a 0x48-byte map node
map node: key string at +0x20 (SSO inline at +0x30 when len <= 15, heap via _M_create when len > 15, NUL at +0x30+len), value u64 = sequence at +0x40, header +0x00..+0x1f

merge.rule: when the iterator is exhausted the node's map is REPLACED by the local map; the old tree is freed with the type's tree-free routine
merge.node_empty: adopt the local tree into the node map (no free)
merge.local_empty: move the node tree to the local header, zero the node map, free the tree
merge.both_nonempty: swap the two headers, free the old node tree
merge.empty_iterator_first_check: when slot 0x10 is false before any entry, the flag is cleared and the routine returns WITHOUT the merge (the node map is left untouched)

version_keys.note: both tables live in BSS and are built by the static initializer 0x606f950 from the literals via the string constructor 0x5f204e0; the initializer is registered at 0x63f3990 (.init_array entry, stored qword at file offset 0x7468)

locked_lookup.returns: 1 on hit, 0 otherwise (also 0 without locking when either out pointer is null)
locked_lookup.lock: instrumented acquire 0x606ca40 on source+0x988, unlock wrapper 0x60d52f0 on every path
locked_lookup.tree: root at source+0xcb0, sentinel &source+0xca8; nodes carry key +0x20, left +0x10, right +0x18, map +0x28
locked_lookup.hit: first node with key in [rsi, rdx): *out1 = its key, map_copy(out2, node+0x28)
locked_lookup.miss: no write to the out pointers

map_copy.rule: deep-copy the map at src+0x00 into the map at dst+0x08 (old dst tree cleared first)

lower_bound.returns: (parent, insert_pos): insert_pos 0 means the key already exists (caller frees the new node), insert_pos == header means insert at the end
lower_bound.comparator: 0x5d498c0: memcmp on the common prefix, else the length difference clamped to int32

tree_free.note: 0x606c280 and 0x606def0 are the same recursive tree-free routine instantiated twice; the only differing instruction is the self-recursive call target. Both are safe no-ops on a null root.

not_claimed: the concrete dynamic type behind the source object's vtable slots (0x198 produce, 0x28 seek, 0x10 has-current, 0x48 current key, 0x50 current value, 0x38 advance, 0x8 release)
what the slot-0x50 value view contains beyond its pinned use (copied into a string and decimal-parsed into the map value)
the owner object's identity and its slot-0x38 dispatch beyond the slot-7 copy that the caller performs
what the flag byte at source+0x4c9 means beyond selecting node type A (0) versus B (nonzero)
who fills node +0x50/+0x54/+0x58 in flows other than this one (they are zero in the caller-built node, so slot 7 resets the owner header here)
the other three vtables whose slots hold the caller 0x5d4cc80 (slots 0x64cb540, 0x64cba20, 0x64cc020)
behaviour on a null owner or a null source pointer (the caller reads source+0x4c9 unconditionally)
the sibling routine 0x606e3a0, which shares the bound getter and the version-key table (not mapped here)
whether the slot-0x50 decimal parse can throw inside the insert loop (the parser throws invalid_argument/out_of_range on malformed input; no handler is pinned in the insert)
